Edition · Tuesday, November 24, 2026 · PM issue

Every price in this issue was checked live on Tuesday, November 24, 2026 — all nine desks verified in a single evening window, 9:20–9:51 PM MST. The board grows from 111 deals to 127 (65 watches, 62 cigars). Headlines: a new Hamilton Jazzmaster Thinline H38525721 at $356.15 after PRE15 (−64.9% vs WatchMaxx $1,014) and a new Breitling Avenger B01 Black AB0146101B1A1 at $3,150 after LUX600 (−48.8% vs Prestige $6,150). The Tissot PRX Powermatic 80 Blue (T137.407.11.041.00) holds at $575.68 at Jomashop — BOLDFS20 cart-verified on the blue itself again, list down to $595.68 — so the out-of-pocket math after $150 in Jomashop gift cards stays ~$425.68. The Aikon Tide family reshuffles: the Orange prints $143 after ML200 at −71.2% against a single-Japan-seller eBay comp — thin, and flagged on its card — while the light-pink EEEE1 ($132) and mint-green CCCC1 ($134) colorways join, the CCCC1 comp using the $152 top of the eBay range, also flagged. Mid-range adds an Oris Divers Sixty-Five Green at $1,350 after ORIS400 (−34.8%); luxury drops the Top Time Thunderbird and Premier B01, whose WatchMaxx streets now match Jomashop exactly. On the investment desk, still nine listings, a new 2023 full-set Daytona 116500LN at $26,300 from Gamzo & Co. (−6.1%) is the cleanest Daytona in the scan, and the truest like-for-like discount remains the white-dial AP Royal Oak 15510ST.OO.1320ST.03 at $43,656 from Romeo Segnatempo (−9.1%, full set, Good condition, thin seller history disclosed); the Daytona 116500LN at $23,036 (−23.1%) and the Submariner 126610LN at $12,574 (−10.2%) are measured against full-set comps while watch-only and box-only respectively — flagged, not like-for-like, on their cards. On cigars, Famous Smoke's sale ends November 25 and cut every Melanio street comp — the AM −38.8% Maduro 10-pack cluster is now ~15.9% — while Thompson now beats Atlantic on the Melanio Torpedo ($89.99 vs $102.04) and the Maduro Torpedo and Churchill ($100.79 vs $102.04), Weekly Special ends 11/29/26; a Montecristo No. 2 Torpedo 5-pack is $29.40 at JR Cigar (−74% vs Famous ~$112.99; caveat: Famous's 5-pack is the Yellow No. 2 line); and two CigarBid Deadwood lots are watchlist-only — the Toro (lot 5952608, all-in $62.00, −40.4%, closes Wednesday, November 25, 9:57 PM ET) and the new Robusto (lot 5954220, all-in $48.50, −50.5%, closes Saturday, November 28, 10:09 PM ET). Cigars Direct's Black Friday sale starts Thursday, November 26 (25% off), so FIRST15 prices must be re-checked after that. Coupons verified this run: BOLDFS20 cart-verified on the PRX Blue itself; PRE15 and FIRST15 cart-tested; ML200, BFWK10, WMBF2026, ORIS400 and the LUX/BRL codes display-verified (WMBF2026 also cart-tested as not applicable to the Blue MOP and the Green Steel Aquis); Thompson's SHIP4FREE banner-verified; Fox's SAVE10 advertised only, not tested. Availability note. Sixty-two desk entries were price-checked for this issue — verified live Tuesday evening, November 24, 2026 across Atlantic Cigar, Cigar Outlet, CigarBid, Cigars.com, Cigars Direct, Famous Smoke Shop, Fox Cigar, JR Cigar and Thompson Cigar. Discounts use live street prices only. The two CigarBid lots are watchlist-only: their prices are all-in at bid-to-win (bid + $7.50 shipping) and their discounts are measured on that all-in figure against JR Cigar — a bid-to-win is never a buyable price and rises before close. Collectible ≠ guaranteed return

The investment desk is an asking-price snapshot, not a resale forecast. Each listing names its comparison source and shows condition and completeness where the scan confirmed them.

Price integrityThe investment desk names its comparison basis on every card — this issue's nine investment listings are named in full: the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak 15510ST.OO.1320ST.08 grey dial at $46,500 from R&R Watches Inc via Chrono24 (full set, 2020) against the $48,500 grey-dial cluster — 4.1%, like-for-like; the Rolex Submariner Date 126610LN at $12,574 from Watches & Luxury via Chrono24 (original box only, no papers, 2020) against the ~$14,000 full-set cluster — 10.2%, FLAGGED: box-only against a full-set comp, not like-for-like; the Rolex Cosmograph Daytona 116500LN at $23,036 from Comptoir d'achats via Chrono24 (watch only, no box or papers, black dial, approx. 2016) against the $29,974 full-set figure — 23.1%, FLAGGED: watch-only against a full-set comp, and $29,974 sits above the current full-set cluster, not like-for-like; the Patek Philippe Nautilus 5711/1A-010 at $110,011 from Watches & Luxury via Chrono24 (original box only, no papers, approx. 2010) against the $115,000 full-set figure — 4.3%, FLAGGED: the item needs procurement, carries no papers, and the comp was not re-verified this run (Chrono24 redirect loop); the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak 15510ST.OO.1320ST.03 white dial at $44,500 from Professor Wrist via Chrono24 (full set) against the ~$48,000 full-set cluster — 7.3%, like-for-like; the same reference at $43,656 from Romeo Segnatempo via Chrono24 (full set, 2022, Good condition with visible wear; not a Trusted Seller and the thinnest seller record in the scan, disclosed on its card) against the same ~$48,000 cluster — 9.1%, like-for-like and the desk's truest investment discount this run; the Rolex Submariner Date 126610LN at $13,250 from Gamzo & Co. via Chrono24 (2023 full set) against the ~$14,000 full-set cluster — 5.4%, like-for-like; and the new Rolex Cosmograph Daytona 116500LN at $26,300 from Gamzo & Co. via Chrono24 (2023 full set) against the $28,000 full-set cluster — 6.1%, like-for-like, the cleanest Daytona deal in the scan. No appreciation is promised on any of them.
LiquidityEstimate how broad the resale market is and how quickly similar pieces actually move.
CompletenessBox, papers, original parts and service records can matter disproportionately.
Ownership dragBuyer premium, tax, servicing, insurance and selling fees belong in the thesis.

Market data, not financial advice. No appreciation claims. Watches are illiquid collectibles; values can fall, provenance can be wrong, and servicing can erase an apparent discount.

Liquidity, defined. Each watch carries the Ledger's liquidity read — High: deep resale market, typically sells in days at market price; Good: active market, typically sells in weeks at a fair price; Thin: narrow buyer pool, longer to sell. It's an editorial assessment from comparable listings, price band, and condition — a guide to how fast you could get out, not a resale guarantee.
